newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia private sector raised more funds in 1Qtr.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia private sector raised more funds in 1Qtr.

text.p: The Malaysian private sector raised net funds totalling 7.4 billion ringgit in the first quarter of 1997, against 5.4 billion in the preceding quarter, the central bank said on Friday.

The funds raised included those from new issues of private debt securities which were boosted by the 1.1 billion ringgit issue of Islamic bonds by Kuala Lumpur International Airport, Bank Negara said in its quarterly report on economic conditions.
"In addition, new funds raised through the stock market were higher, totalling 3.6 billion ringgit," the statement said. No comparative figure was given.

Net long-term funds raised in the capital market amounted to 5.4 billion ringgit in the first quarter, 4.0 percent compared to the preceding quarter, and 45 percent down from the same quarter a year ago.
"This was attributed mainly to the large redemptions of Malaysian Government Securities and Government Investment Issues totalling 2.0 billion ringgit," the statement said.

Malaysia's loan approvals in the first quarter of this year stood at 50.2 billion ringgit, about half of which was granted to the broad property and finance, insurance and business services sectors, the central bank said.
The quarterly figure compared with 50.8 billion in the last quarter of 1996.
